children: India’s central bank governor Sanjay Malhotra urged fintech firms to safeguard customer data and strengthen cybersecurity as artificial intelligence plays a growing role in finance.

AI can pose challenges ranging from bias and exclusion to cybersecurity threats, data privacy concerns and an erosion of human judgment, Malhotra said at the Global Fintech Fest in Mumbai on Thursday. Addressing those risks is “extremely important for maintaining consumer trust,” he said.
Protecting that trust also requires firms to handle customer information responsibly. “I would urge all of you to treat data as a fiduciary responsibility, not as a business asset,” Malhotra said.

Banks are increasingly using AI agents to automate operations and customer service, while algorithms are being deployed to monitor risk, detect fraud and assess borrowers. The rapid adoption is helping cut costs but is also raising regulatory worries over data protection, cybersecurity and reliance on a small group of technology providers.

The RBI is also scrutinizing broader technology risks. On Wednesday, Malhotra’s deputy Rohit Jain flagged banks’ dependence on a small number of common technology providers as a potential threat to financial stability.

Malhotra said large firms should aim to be “not just too big to fail, but too significant to be careless.” He also urged fintech companies not to exploit regulatory gaps or expand rapidly without first seeking clarity from regulators.
“Regulation and innovation are not opposing forces, but they are mutually reinforcing pillars of a resilient financial ecosystem,” Malhotra said.

title: RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra urges fintech firms to strengthen data protection, cybersecurity
